intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace while dressed in traditional Hanbok attire. Hanbok rental shops are located just outside the palace gates, making it easy to combine both activities. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 after settling in, and best done in the morning to avoid crowds. Stay nearby in Jongno-gu to walk directly to the palace.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). The market is lively and authentic, offering a true local food experience without tourist markup. Book a guided food tour or explore independently. Stay in Jongno-gu or Euljiro for easy access.

experiences.name: Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-pop and youth culture hub. Hongdae is packed with indie music venues, K-pop dance studios offering drop-in classes, street performers, quirky cafes, and K-beauty shops. Join a K-pop dance class at a local studio for around $15–20, then explore the nightlife and street art. This area is best experienced in the late afternoon through evening when energy peaks.

experiences.name: Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil, an artsy courtyard mall with local designers and handmade goods. Stop at a traditional Korean tea house to try omija tea or sikhye. This culturally rich neighborhood is walkable from Gyeongbokgung and Gwangjang Market, making it perfect for a combined day out. Ideal for mid-trip exploration.

experiences.name: Korean BBQ Dinner Experience in Mapo-gu
experiences.description: Enjoy an authentic Korean BBQ dinner at a local grill restaurant in the Mapo-gu area near Hongdae or Hapjeong. Order samgyeopsal (pork belly) or galbi (beef short ribs), grilled tableside and wrapped in lettuce with ssamjang paste. Pair with unlimited banchan side dishes and soju or makgeolli. This is a quintessential Korean dining ritual best enjoyed with a group. Staying in Mapo-gu puts you steps away from top BBQ spots.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or limousine bus to Bupyeong Station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Grab a late-night snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) to unwind after the flight.

meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Convenience store snacks near the hotel (tteokbokki cup, triangle kimbap, ramen) — approx ₩3,000–6,000

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a T-money card at the airport or Bupyeong Station for easy transit use throughout the trip. AREX to Bupyeong area costs roughly ₩4,150. Dress warmly — December temperatures hover around 3°C at night.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy the complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn (included with most rooms). Explore the Bupyeong Modoo Mall underground shopping complex near the hotel — one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for budget K-fashion browsing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Bupyeong Cultural Street and Bupyeong Market for a taste of local Incheon life. Browse street stalls and pick up affordable snacks. Visit the nearby Bupyeong Park for a short winter walk and to get oriented with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Bupyeong's local restaurant alleys for dinner. Try a local Korean BBQ spot or a sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) restaurant to warm up. Return to the hotel early to plan the Seoul day trips ahead.

meals.lunch: Bupyeong Market street food — tteokbokki, sundae, hotteok — approx ₩5,000–8,000
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood restaurant — sundubu jjigae set meal approx ₩8,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a gentle orientation day. Bupyeong is well-connected via subway Line 1 and Line 7, making Seoul very accessible. Stock up on snacks at the convenience store for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 1 from Bupyeong to Seoul Station (approx 40 min, ₩1,550). Walk to Gyeongbokgung Palace — the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Arrive early for the 10:00 Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony at Gwanghwamun Gate. Admission is ₩3,000 (free with hanbok rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace grounds (free entry). Walk to Bukchon Hanok Village — a stunning neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the narrow alleys and enjoy the contrast of old and new Seoul. Visit Gyeongbokgung's Heungnyemun Gate area for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong for dinner and evening exploration. Browse the Ssamziegil courtyard complex for K-culture souvenirs and indie shops. Enjoy the festive winter street atmosphere with street food vendors.

meals.lunch: Insadong street food or a local kimbap restaurant near Gyeongbokgung — approx ₩6,000–9,000
meals.dinner: Insadong traditional Korean restaurant — bibimbap or doenjang jjigae set — approx ₩9,000–12,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear very warm layers — Gyeongbokgung is exposed and windy in December. Renting a hanbok (₩10,000–15,000/hr) grants free palace entry and makes for great photos in the snow-dusted courtyards.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Hongdae area (transfer at Sindorim to Line 2, approx 50 min). Explore Hongdae's famous street art murals and indie culture scene in the morning when it's less crowded. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or just enjoy the free outdoor art installations and painted walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Yonsei University campus — beautiful architecture and a popular K-drama filming location. Head to Sinchon for budget shopping and local student-area eats. Browse the many affordable clothing stores and K-pop merchandise shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the vibrant Friday night street performance scene. Buskers and K-pop cover dance groups often perform near Hongdae Exit 9. Browse the night market stalls and enjoy the youthful K-culture energy.

meals.lunch: Sinchon student area — dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) restaurant approx ₩9,000–11,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food — corn dogs, tteokbokki, gyeranppang (egg bread) — approx ₩6,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in Hongdae are lively but can be crowded. Keep belongings secure. Many K-pop idol agency buildings (JYP, etc.) are in this area — a treat for K-culture fans. Most street performances are free.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Myeongdong (Line 4, approx 55 min from Bupyeong). Visit Myeongdong Cathedral — a stunning Gothic Catholic church and Seoul landmark, free to enter. Explore the surrounding streets before the shopping crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into Myeongdong's famous street food alley — one of Seoul's best street food experiences. Try lobster grilled cheese, tornado potato, and Korean fried chicken skewers. Browse affordable K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude House, The Face Shop) for budget skincare and cosmetics.
day_by_day.evening: Walk uphill to Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower). Take the cable car (₩9,500 round trip) or hike up for free. Enjoy the panoramic night view of Seoul — spectacular in winter. See the famous love locks on the fence around the tower.

meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food stalls — approx ₩8,000–12,000 for a satisfying spread
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja (famous local restaurant) — kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) or mandu (dumplings) approx ₩9,000–11,000

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely popular on weekends. Go early for a calmer experience. K-beauty products are significantly cheaper here than abroad — great for budget gift shopping. Namsan Tower is magical in winter with city lights.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Dongdaemun History & Culture Park (Line 4 or 5). Visit the iconic Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark with free outdoor access and often free exhibitions inside. Walk along the Cheonggyecheon Stream nearby — a peaceful urban waterway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Gwangjang Market — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. This is a must for local food lovers. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare) at the market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun shopping district for evening browsing. The massive shopping malls (Doota, Migliore) are open late. Browse affordable K-fashion and accessories. The area is especially atmospheric at night with neon lights.

meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok + mayak kimbap + makgeolli (rice wine) — approx ₩10,000–15,000
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area pojangmacha (street tent restaurant) — odeng (fish cake soup) and tteokbokki — approx ₩6,000–9,000

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is one of the most authentic food experiences in Seoul — featured on Netflix's Street Food Asia. Bring cash as many stalls don't accept cards. Cheonggyecheon Stream has winter light festivals in December.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Itaewon (Line 6). Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — world-class Korean art collection with free or low-cost entry for some sections. Walk up to Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood for a local, less-touristy Itaewon experience with great street art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon's multicultural streets and the famous Antique Furniture Street. Walk to Gyeongnidan-gil — a trendy alley with independent cafes, vintage shops, and unique eateries. Great for K-culture and contemporary Seoul vibes.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hannam-dong for a stroll through one of Seoul's most stylish neighborhoods. Window-shop along the boutique-lined streets. Return to Bupyeong via subway for a relaxed evening.

meals.lunch: Gyeongnidan-gil cafe or small restaurant — pasta or Korean fusion — approx ₩10,000–13,000
meals.dinner: Itaewon local Korean restaurant — samgyeopsal (pork belly BBQ) — approx ₩12,000–15,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Monday is a good day to visit museums as weekend crowds thin out. Itaewon has a very international feel — great for experiencing Seoul's multicultural side. Gyeongnidan-gil is a favorite among young Seoulites and K-culture enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Jongno 3-ga area. Visit Changdeokgung Palace (₩3,000) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and arguably the most beautiful of Seoul's palaces. The Secret Garden (Huwon) tour is available for an additional fee (₩5,000) — highly recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Changgyeonggung Palace (₩1,000) next door — less crowded and equally beautiful. Then explore the nearby Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendy neighborhood of converted hanok buildings housing cafes, vintage shops, and galleries. Very photogenic and K-culture rich.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Jongno's Tapgol Park — historically significant as the site of the 1919 Independence Movement. Walk along Pimatgol Alley — a historic narrow lane with traditional Korean restaurants that have served locals for centuries.

meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong hanok cafe — traditional sikhye (rice punch) and Korean snacks — approx ₩8,000–11,000
meals.dinner: Pimatgol Alley traditional restaurant — galbitang (short rib soup) or seolleongtang (ox bone soup) — approx ₩10,000–13,000

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung's Secret Garden is one of Seoul's most serene spots — especially beautiful with winter frost on the traditional pavilions. Book the Secret Garden tour in advance online as spots are limited. Ikseon-dong is extremely photogenic for K-culture content.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Gangnam (Line 2, approx 1 hr from Bupyeong). Visit COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. Don't miss the stunning Starfield Library inside COEX — a massive public bookshelf installation that's free to visit and very photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Bongeunsa Temple — a 1,200-year-old Buddhist temple dramatically situated amid Gangnam's skyscrapers. Free to enter. Experience the peaceful temple atmosphere and learn about Korean Buddhism. Walk along Teheran-ro to experience the contrast of modern Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gangnam's Garosu-gil (Tree-lined Road) — a chic street with boutiques, cafes, and restaurants. Window-shop and enjoy a budget-friendly dinner at one of the many affordable Korean restaurants in the side streets off Garosu-gil.

meals.lunch: COEX food court — various Korean options — approx ₩8,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Gangnam side street Korean restaurant — jeyuk bokkeum (spicy pork stir-fry) with rice — approx ₩9,000–12,000

day_by_day.notes: Bongeunsa Temple offers templestay programs if interested in a deeper cultural experience (book in advance). The Starfield Library is free and one of Seoul's most Instagrammable spots. Gangnam is pricier overall — stick to side streets for budget dining.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Sinchon/Ewha area. Visit Ewha Womans University — famous for its stunning glass-and-stone campus architecture (the ECC building is iconic). The surrounding Ewha shopping street has very affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Yonsei University campus for more beautiful architecture and a walk through the historic grounds. Then explore the Sinchon underground shopping area for budget K-pop merchandise and fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Head to Myeongdong or City Hall Plaza to experience the spectacular Christmas lights and decorations. Seoul City Hall's outdoor skating rink (₩1,000 entry + ₩5,000 skate rental) is a magical Christmas Eve activity. Enjoy the festive street food and atmosphere.

meals.lunch: Sinchon area — affordable Korean set meal at a local restaurant — approx ₩8,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Christmas street food and festive stalls — approx ₩10,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of Seoul's biggest celebration nights — couples and friends fill the streets. The city is beautifully decorated. Book any restaurant dinner in advance if you want a sit-down meal as popular spots fill up. The atmosphere is incredibly festive and very K-drama-esque.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul, free entry. On Christmas Day, the contrast of Buddhist and Christian celebrations in Seoul is fascinating. The temple is beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) area — the former presidential residence opened to the public in 2022. Free entry with online reservation. Walk along the scenic Bugaksan mountain trail behind it for stunning winter views of Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lotte World Tower area in Jamsil. Admire the 555m skyscraper (one of the world's tallest) from outside. Visit Lotte World Mall's food basement for an incredible array of affordable Korean food options. Enjoy the Christmas Day atmosphere.

meals.lunch: Near Jogyesa Temple — Buddhist temple food restaurant (사찰음식) — approx ₩10,000–13,000
meals.dinner: Lotte World Mall basement food court — Korean fried chicken, kimbap, or hot pot — approx ₩9,000–13,000

day_by_day.notes: The Blue House (Cheong Wa Dae) requires advance online reservation — book several days ahead. Christmas Day in Seoul is a public holiday — some smaller shops may be closed but major attractions remain open. The Lotte World Tower observation deck (₩27,000) is optional for those wanting a splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Mapo-gu area. Visit Mangwon Market — a local neighborhood market beloved by Seoulites and far less touristy than Gwangjang. Excellent for authentic local food and produce browsing. Try fresh hotteok (sweet pancakes) and various banchan (side dishes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Hangang River at Mangwon Hangang Park. The winter riverside scenery is beautiful and peaceful. Rent a bicycle (₩3,000/hr) if weather permits, or simply walk along the river path. Visit the nearby World Cup Park for a quiet nature escape within the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Hongdae for a final evening of K-culture immersion. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) — a quintessential Korean experience. Budget noraebangs in Hongdae cost approximately ₩10,000–15,000 per hour per room. End the night with Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek).

meals.lunch: Mangwon Market — fresh market food, kimbap, and snacks — approx ₩7,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae chimaek (chicken + beer) restaurant — approx ₩15,000–20,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Mangwon Market is a hidden gem — very authentic and local. The Hangang riverside in winter is serene and beautiful, especially on clear days with mountain views. Norebang is a must-do K-culture experience — most rooms are private so it's comfortable even for shy singers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit any favorite spots near Bupyeong or do last-minute souvenir shopping at Bupyeong Modoo Mall underground shopping center. Pick up Korean snacks, instant ramyeon, and K-beauty products as gifts. Enjoy a final Korean breakfast at a local restaurant near the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Toyoko Inn. Store luggage at the hotel if needed. Take a final stroll through Bupyeong neighborhood. Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or limousine bus (allow 60–90 minutes travel time). Complete check-in and departure procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Korean snacks, cosmetics, and souvenirs at airport prices.

meals.breakfast: Local Korean restaurant near hotel — haejang-guk (hangover soup) or congee — approx ₩7,000–9,000
meals.lunch: Incheon Airport food court — bibimbap or Korean set meal — approx ₩10,000–13,000
meals.dinner: Airport or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport check-in — Incheon is large and security lines can be long on weekends. The airport has excellent duty-free shopping for Korean snacks (Choco Pie, Pepero, Honey Butter Chips) and cosmetics. T-money card balance can be refunded at airport convenience stores (small fee applies).

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage. Take Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or limousine bus to Bupyeong area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Grab a late-night snack near the hotel.

meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store meal (GS25 or CU near hotel) — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, and hot drinks. Budget: ~5,000–8,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Bupyeong is well-connected via subway Line 1 and Line 7. Exchange some currency at the airport for convenience. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip. Dress warmly — December temperatures average around 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. After a leisurely breakfast, explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall and Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center — one of Korea's largest underground markets, great for affordable K-fashion and accessories. Walk around Bupyeong-gu neighborhood to get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take subway Line 1 to Incheon Chinatown (Incheon Station). Explore Korea's only Chinatown, visit Jayu Park for panoramic views, and walk across the colorful Incheon Open Port area with its historic Japanese and Chinese colonial architecture. Visit the Incheon Open Port Museum (admission ~1,000 KRW).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong area. Explore Bupyeong Rodeo Street for evening street food and shopping. Enjoy the local nightlife atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby bakery — Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours. Budget: ~5,000–8,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Incheon Chinatown specialty — Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) at a local Chinese-Korean restaurant. This dish originated in Incheon's Chinatown. Budget: ~8,000–12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Bupyeong Rodeo Street pojangmacha (street food stall) — try tteokbokki, sundae, and hotteok. Budget: ~10,000–15,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Incheon Chinatown is about 20 minutes from Bupyeong by subway. Wear layers — it will be cold. Jayu Park may be icy so wear appropriate footwear. Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center is open until 8–9 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway to Seoul (about 40–50 min from Bupyeong via Line 1 to Jonggak or City Hall). Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace — Korea's grandest Joseon-era palace. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM. Admission: 3,000 KRW. Consider renting a hanbok (traditional dress) for free palace entry and great photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Bukchon Hanok Village — a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the winding alleys and enjoy the contrast of old architecture against the modern city skyline. Then visit Insadong Street for K-culture souvenirs, traditional crafts, and art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square to see the illuminated statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Enjoy the winter light installations. Then explore Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully lit urban stream perfect for an evening stroll.

meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongshik lite) near Insadong — try Sanchon or a local restaurant. Budget: ~12,000–18,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market nearby — try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap, and yukhoe (beef tartare). Budget: ~12,000–20,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rental shops are clustered near the palace entrance (around 10,000–20,000 KRW for 2 hours). Bukchon can be slippery in winter — wear non-slip shoes. Gwangjang Market is one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic markets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) — take the cable car up for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Attach a love lock on the fence and enjoy the observation deck. Cable car: ~12,000 KRW round trip; Tower admission: ~21,000 KRW. Alternatively, hike up Namsan for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and explore Myeongdong — Seoul's most famous shopping and K-beauty district. Browse cosmetics shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), try street food, and soak in the vibrant K-culture atmosphere. Visit Myeongdong Cathedral, a stunning Gothic landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeongdong for dinner and evening shopping. The street food stalls are especially lively on Friday evenings. Explore Lotte Department Store or Lotte Young Plaza for K-fashion and pop culture merchandise.

meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food feast — egg bread (계란빵), tornado potato, Korean fried chicken skewers, and hotteok. Budget: ~10,000–15,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja — famous for kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings). Iconic, affordable, and delicious. Budget: ~9,000–14,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely popular on Friday evenings. Olive Young is a must-visit for K-beauty products at reasonable prices. The cable car to Namsan may have queues — arrive early. December views from the tower are spectacular on clear days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic architectural landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. Check out the Dongdaemun Market area for fabric, fashion, and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the epicenter of Korean youth culture, indie music, and street art. Explore the vibrant street art murals, browse independent boutiques, and visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends Store for K-pop culture immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the Saturday night atmosphere — live busking performances, club previews, and street performances are common. Explore the nightlife-friendly streets and enjoy the youthful energy.

meals.lunch: Dongdaemun area — try a local Korean BBQ lunch set (삼겹살 samgyeopsal). Budget: ~13,000–18,000 KRW per person
meals.dinner: Hongdae — try Yoogane Dak Galbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or a trendy Korean fusion restaurant. Budget: ~12,000–18,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: DDP hosts rotating exhibitions — check their website for current shows. Hongdae is best experienced in the afternoon and evening when the street performers and vendors are most active. Dongdaemun wholesale markets are open late (some 24 hours) if you want to shop for fashion deals.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Beautifully decorated with lanterns, especially festive in December. Free entry. Then walk to nearby Unhyeongung Palace, a smaller and less-crowded royal residence with interesting history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Samcheong-dong — a charming neighborhood of art galleries, indie cafés, and boutique shops connecting Gyeongbokgung to Bukchon. Browse the galleries and enjoy the quiet, artistic atmosphere. Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea (free with Gyeongbokgung ticket).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Anguk area for a traditional Korean tea ceremony experience at a hanok tea house. Enjoy the peaceful ambiance with a warm cup of traditional Korean tea (omija, barley, or green tea).

meals.lunch: Samcheong-dong café lunch — try a Korean-style brunch at one of the charming hanok cafés. Budget: ~12,000–16,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Insadong area — try Tosokchon Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), a warming and nourishing winter dish. Budget: ~17,000–20,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is particularly beautiful in winter with its lantern decorations. Samcheong-dong can be hilly and icy — wear appropriate footwear. Tosokchon is very popular and may have a queue — arrive before 6 PM to avoid long waits.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway. Walk along the impressive fortress walls surrounding the old city. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace within the fortress grounds. Admission: ~1,500 KRW.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market area near the fortress. Visit the Suwon Ibi Market or Paldalmun Gate area. Enjoy the local atmosphere and pick up traditional snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Relax at the hotel or explore a local jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) near Bupyeong for a traditional Korean wellness experience. Budget: ~10,000–15,000 KRW.

meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — a regional specialty the city is famous for. Try a local restaurant near the fortress. Budget: ~15,000–25,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Bupyeong local restaurant — try doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) set meal. Budget: ~8,000–12,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress is about 1 hour from Bupyeong via subway (Line 1 direct). The fortress walls offer great winter views but can be windy and cold — dress very warmly. The jjimjilbang is a quintessential Korean cultural experience — bring a change of clothes and a small towel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. Free admission. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the permanent collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Itaewon — Seoul's most international neighborhood. Explore the diverse restaurants, vintage clothing shops, and antique stores. Visit Leeum Samsung Museum of Art for world-class contemporary and traditional Korean art (admission ~10,000 KRW).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Haebangchon (HBC) or Gyeongnidan-gil — trendy streets near Itaewon with independent restaurants, craft beer bars, and unique cafés. Great for an eclectic evening experience.

meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria or nearby — try a Korean bibimbap set. Budget: ~10,000–14,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Itaewon or Gyeongnidan-gil — try a Korean-fusion restaurant or authentic international cuisine. Budget: ~15,000–22,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays — Tuesday is perfect. Itaewon is very walkable from Yongsan. Leeum Museum has a stunning building designed by three world-renowned architects. Gyeongnidan-gil has become a foodie hotspot with many Instagram-worthy spots.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks in Jamsil. Enjoy rides, the folk museum, and the magical indoor/outdoor park experience. December is especially festive with Christmas decorations. Day pass: ~62,000 KRW.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Lotte World or take a break to visit Seokchon Lake nearby — beautifully decorated for the Christmas season with light installations. Walk around the lake and enjoy the festive atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jamsil's COEX Mall — a massive underground shopping complex with an aquarium, bookstore (Starfield Library), and countless shops and restaurants. Enjoy the Christmas decorations and evening shopping.

meals.lunch: Lotte World food court — try Korean fried chicken or a Korean rice bowl. Budget: ~10,000–15,000 KRW
meals.dinner: COEX Mall food hall — wide variety of Korean and international options. Try Korean BBQ or a Korean stew restaurant. Budget: ~15,000–22,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World can be crowded in December — arrive early. The outdoor Magic Island section may be cold but is beautifully decorated. COEX Starfield Library is a stunning architectural space worth visiting even if you don't shop. Book Lotte World tickets online in advance for discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Secret Garden tour must be booked in advance (admission ~8,000 KRW). The palace grounds are beautiful in winter with snow-dusted traditional architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendy neighborhood of restored hanok buildings converted into stylish cafés, restaurants, and boutiques. Very popular for its blend of traditional architecture and modern culture. Perfect for Christmas Eve afternoon strolling.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul — head to Myeongdong or Gangnam for the festive atmosphere. Seoul celebrates Christmas with elaborate light displays, street performances, and a lively holiday atmosphere. Visit a rooftop bar or café for a special Christmas Eve view.

meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong — try a trendy Korean café lunch or traditional Korean food in a hanok setting. Budget: ~12,000–18,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — try a Korean BBQ restaurant for a celebratory meal. Recommended: Maple Tree House or a mid-range Korean BBQ in Myeongdong. Budget: ~25,000–35,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour well in advance — it sells out quickly. Christmas Eve in Seoul is very festive and busy — expect crowds in popular areas. Many restaurants offer special Christmas menus. Ikseon-dong is extremely photogenic and perfect for K-culture enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park — a stunning mountain park within Seoul city limits. Take a moderate hike to Bukhansanseong Fortress for incredible panoramic views of Seoul in winter. The snow-capped peaks are breathtaking. Admission: ~1,600 KRW.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit Seodaemun Prison History Hall — a sobering but important museum documenting Korea's independence movement during Japanese colonial rule. Admission: ~3,000 KRW. Then explore the nearby Sinchon area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam district for the evening — explore Garosu-gil (tree-lined street) with its boutique shops and cafés, and experience the upscale side of Seoul's K-culture scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — Christmas morning treat yourself to a nice breakfast
meals.lunch: Post-hike warm meal near Bukhansan — try a hearty sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant. Budget: ~9,000–13,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Gangnam — Garosu-gil restaurant. Try a modern Korean cuisine restaurant for a Christmas dinner treat. Budget: ~20,000–30,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan can be icy and snowy in December — bring hiking poles if possible and wear waterproof boots. The hike to Bukhansanseong takes about 2–3 hours round trip at a moderate pace. Christmas Day is a public holiday in Korea — most attractions are open but some smaller shops may be closed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan — a powerful and comprehensive museum documenting Korean military history and the Korean War. Free admission. The outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and warships. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Mangwon Market — a local neighborhood market beloved by Seoulites for its authentic, non-touristy atmosphere. Browse fresh produce, street food, and local goods. Then explore the trendy Mangwon-dong and Hapjeong neighborhoods along the Han River.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Yeouido Hangang Park for a Han River evening experience. In winter, the park has ice skating rinks and festive lighting. Try the famous Han River convenience store picnic experience (buy food from GS25 and eat by the river — a beloved Korean cultural activity even in winter).

meals.lunch: Mangwon Market street food — try pajeon (green onion pancake), tteokbokki, and fresh fish cake soup. Budget: ~8,000–12,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Yeouido area — try a Korean chicken and beer (chimaek) restaurant, a beloved Korean food culture combination. Budget: ~15,000–22,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Mangwon Market is best on weekends when it's most lively. The Han River ice skating rink at Yeouido is open in December (skate rental available). Hapjeong and Mangwon are increasingly trendy neighborhoods with great independent cafés and restaurants worth exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit any favorite spots or do last-minute shopping. Head to Namdaemun Market — Seoul's largest traditional market, open since 1414. Great for affordable souvenirs, Korean snacks, clothing, and accessories. Try the famous Namdaemun kalguksu alley for a farewell breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Deoksugung Palace — centrally located and beautiful in winter. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:30 AM, 2:00 PM, 3:30 PM). Walk the Deoksugung Stonewall Walkway (Doldamgil) — a romantic and scenic path. Admission: ~1,000 KRW. Do final souvenir shopping in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Enjoy a farewell dinner near the hotel. Pack and prepare for departure. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of K-culture, food, and exploration.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market — kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) at the famous noodle alley. Budget: ~7,000–10,000 KRW
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Deoksugung — try a Korean dosirak (lunchbox) café or a simple bibimbap restaurant. Budget: ~10,000–14,000 KRW
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner near Bupyeong hotel — try a full Korean BBQ experience (pork belly samgyeopsal with all the banchan side dishes). Budget: ~15,000–25,000 KRW

day_by_day.notes: Namdaemun Market opens early — great for a morning visit. Pack any purchased food items carefully for the journey home (check customs regulations). Return T-money card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security at Incheon. The AREX train from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport takes about 43 minutes.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace while dressed in traditional Hanbok attire. Hanbok rental shops are located just outside the palace gates, making it easy to combine both activities. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 after settling in, and best done in the morning to avoid crowds. Stay nearby in Jongno-gu to walk directly to the palace.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). The market is lively and authentic, offering a true local food experience without tourist markup. Book a guided food tour or explore independently. Stay in Jongno-gu or Euljiro for easy access.

experiences.name: Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-pop and youth culture hub. Hongdae is packed with indie music venues, K-pop dance studios offering drop-in classes, street performers, quirky cafes, and K-beauty shops. Join a K-pop dance class at a local studio for around $15–20, then explore the nightlife and street art. This area is best experienced in the late afternoon through evening when energy peaks.

experiences.name: Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil, an artsy courtyard mall with local designers and handmade goods. Stop at a traditional Korean tea house to try omija tea or sikhye. This culturally rich neighborhood is walkable from Gyeongbokgung and Gwangjang Market, making it perfect for a combined day out. Ideal for mid-trip exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.evening: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and take the AREX Express Train or private airport transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Light late-night snack near the hotel if hungry.

meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snack or 24-hour Korean ramen shop near Bupyeong station (Bupyeong is known for its underground shopping and late-night eateries)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30 KST. Allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and transfer. Bupyeong station area has 24-hour convenience stores and pojangmacha (street food stalls). Rest well — the itinerary begins properly tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast, then explore Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center — one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for K-beauty products, fashion, and local goods. Stroll around Bupyeong-gu neighborhood to acclimate to the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway from Bupyeong to central Seoul (approx. 40 min). Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental — dress in traditional Hanbok attire and explore the iconic Joseon-era royal palace. Stroll through the palace grounds, visit Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, and enjoy the winter atmosphere with light snow possibilities.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bukchon Hanok Village for a twilight walk through preserved traditional Korean houses. Enjoy the atmospheric lantern-lit alleyways in the cold winter evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café in Bupyeong
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang — legendary ginseng chicken soup restaurant near Gyeongbokgung, perfect for warming up in winter
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul (2 Michelin stars) in Gangnam — modern Korean cuisine with premium tasting menus showcasing elevated Korean flavors

day_by_day.notes: Hanbok rental shops near Gyeongbokgung open around 9–10am. Book Jungsik in advance as it fills up quickly. Dress in warm layers under the Hanbok — December temperatures average 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The winter-bare trees and frozen ponds create a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere. Guided tours of the Secret Garden are available in English.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Experience — wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil courtyard for artisan goods and unique Korean souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Cheonggyecheon Stream, beautifully lit in the evening. Then head to the Jongno area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Bora in Insadong — famous for its purple taro lattes and Korean-inspired pastries
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang — award-winning Buddhist temple cuisine restaurant near Insadong, offering a serene and refined dining experience
meals.dinner: Mingles (1 Michelin star) — innovative Korean cuisine blending traditional and contemporary techniques in a sophisticated setting

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours at Changdeokgung require advance booking and run at set times. Insadong is walkable from the palace. Cheonggyecheon Stream is beautifully illuminated in winter evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour — dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), and yukhoe (Korean beef tartare). Arrive early for the freshest experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark. Browse design exhibitions, visit the Seoul Museum of Design, and explore the surrounding fashion district. Check out the Dongdaemun History & Culture Park nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Namsan Seoul Tower via cable car for panoramic night views of the glittering Seoul skyline. Visit the observation deck and enjoy the romantic lock wall.

meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market street food feast — budget extra time to sample multiple stalls including the famous raw beef yukhoe and fresh bindaetteok
meals.dinner: Gaon (3 Michelin stars) — the pinnacle of Korean fine dining, offering an exquisite royal court cuisine-inspired tasting menu with exceptional service

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is most vibrant in the morning. Book Gaon well in advance — it is one of Seoul's most prestigious restaurants. Namsan Tower cable car runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an extraordinary collection of Korean artifacts spanning 5,000 years of history. Explore the permanent galleries at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon and the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — a world-class private museum housing both traditional Korean art and contemporary international works in a stunning building designed by three architectural legends.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hongdae K-Culture & Street Performance Walk — immerse yourself in Seoul's vibrant K-pop and youth culture hub. Hongdae is packed with indie music venues, street performers, K-pop merchandise stores, and trendy cafés. Experience the electric Saturday night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Anthracite Coffee Roasters in Itaewon — specialty coffee in a converted factory space, a Seoul institution
meals.lunch: Vatos Urban Tacos in Itaewon — beloved fusion restaurant blending Korean and Mexican flavors with premium ingredients
meals.dinner: Maple Tree House in Itaewon — premium Korean BBQ with USDA prime and Hanwoo beef, elegant private dining rooms

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum may require advance ticket booking for special exhibitions. Hongdae is most vibrant after 7pm on weekends with street performers and pop-up events. Dress warmly for outdoor street performances.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Namsangol Hanok Village — a beautifully restored traditional Korean village at the foot of Namsan Mountain. Explore the five restored aristocratic homes, traditional gardens, and cultural performances.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Myeongdong — Seoul's premier shopping and beauty district. Explore flagship K-beauty stores (Sulwhasoo, Innisfree, Amorepacific), luxury department stores (Lotte, Shinsegae), and sample street food along the main boulevard.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean performance — book tickets for the National Theater of Korea or a Nanta cooking performance show for an entertaining cultural evening.

meals.breakfast: Egg Drop in Myeongdong — premium egg sandwich café beloved by locals and visitors
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — legendary hand-made noodle and dumpling restaurant, a Seoul institution since 1966
meals.dinner: Dooreyoo (1 Michelin star) — refined Korean cuisine with a focus on seasonal ingredients and traditional fermentation techniques

day_by_day.notes: Namsangol Hanok Village is free to enter and offers cultural programs on weekends. Myeongdong is extremely busy on Sundays — visit flagship beauty stores early. Book performance tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Observe morning rituals, admire the ancient trees, and experience the serene contrast between the temple and the bustling city. Explore the Buddhist cultural center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming neighborhood of narrow alleyways, independent galleries, artisan workshops, and traditional hanok cafés. Visit the Gyeomjae Jeong Seon Memorial Hall and browse local art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Gwanghwamun Square area — see the illuminated statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Enjoy the winter light installations that typically decorate the square during December.

meals.breakfast: Café Onion Anguk — a beautifully renovated hanok café serving artisan pastries and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gwanghwamun Gukbap — premium Korean rice soup restaurant beloved by locals for its rich, slow-cooked broth
meals.dinner: La Yeon (3 Michelin stars) at The Shilla Hotel — extraordinary Korean fine dining with breathtaking city views from the 23rd floor

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is particularly atmospheric in the early morning. Seochon Village is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. La Yeon requires advance reservation and smart dress code.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 30 minutes from Seoul by subway. Walk the 5.7km fortress walls, visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, and enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Suwon — visit the Korean Folk Village nearby for an immersive experience of traditional Korean rural life, crafts, and seasonal performances.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and head to Gangnam district — explore the upscale Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong luxury fashion district, home to flagship Korean designer boutiques and international luxury brands.

meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi — Suwon is famous for its distinctive short-rib BBQ style; dine at a traditional galbi restaurant in the city center
meals.dinner: Dosa in Cheongdam-dong — sophisticated modern Korean restaurant in the heart of Gangnam's luxury district

day_by_day.notes: Take Line 1 subway directly to Suwon Station (approx. 50 min from Seoul). The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours. Korean Folk Village is a 15-minute taxi from Suwon Station. Return to Seoul by 6pm for evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan — a powerful and comprehensive museum documenting Korea's military history. The outdoor exhibition of aircraft, tanks, and warships is impressive even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Hannam-dong neighborhood — Seoul's most fashionable enclave with concept stores, art galleries, and design studios. Visit the Hannam-dong antique furniture district and browse independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Korean tea ceremony at O'sulloc Tea House or a private tea ceremony studio in Insadong. Then enjoy a night walk along the Han River at Banpo Bridge to see the famous Rainbow Fountain (seasonal — check availability in December).

meals.breakfast: Fritz Coffee Company in Mapo — one of Seoul's most celebrated specialty coffee roasters
meals.lunch: Hannam-dong Burger — premium Korean-style gourmet burger at one of Hannam's trendy lunch spots
meals.dinner: Soigné (1 Michelin star) — avant-garde tasting menu restaurant in Hannam-dong, blending Korean ingredients with European techniques

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial is free to enter. Hannam-dong is best explored on foot. Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain may not operate in December due to cold — confirm in advance. Soigné requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World — Asia's largest indoor theme park for a festive Christmas Eve experience. Enjoy the elaborate Christmas decorations, ice skating rink, and indoor attractions. Alternatively, visit the adjacent Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory for stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jamsil and the COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. Visit the famous Starfield Library inside COEX, browse luxury boutiques, and explore the aquarium.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve special dinner and celebration. Experience Seoul's festive atmosphere in Myeongdong or Gangnam, where streets are beautifully decorated with Christmas lights and live performances.

meals.lunch: Lotte World Food Court or a café inside Lotte World Tower
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at Nobu Seoul in Lotte World Tower — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion with premium ingredients and festive seasonal menu

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the most festive nights in Seoul — the city transforms with lights and celebrations. Book Christmas Eve dinner well in advance. Lotte World Tower observation deck offers spectacular night views of the city.

day_by_day.morning: Peaceful Christmas morning walk in Olympic Park — one of Seoul's most beautiful parks, featuring outdoor sculptures, walking paths, and the historic Mongchontoseong earthen fortress. Enjoy the crisp winter air and serene atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Arts Center in Seocho — explore the galleries, outdoor sculpture garden, and check for special Christmas Day performances or exhibitions. Browse the arts and crafts market if available.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert or traditional Korean performance at the Seoul Arts Center or National Theater of Korea — many venues host special Christmas Day performances.

meals.breakfast: Tartine Bakery Seoul in Gangnam — premium artisan bakery for a special Christmas morning treat
meals.lunch: Hanwoo Dining Woo Lae Oak — one of Seoul's most historic Korean BBQ restaurants, established in 1946, serving premium Hanwoo beef
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul (2 Michelin stars) — intimate and innovative Korean tasting menu with exceptional seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions have reduced hours on Christmas Day — confirm opening times in advance. Seoul Arts Center and National Theater of Korea typically have special holiday programming. Book dinner reservations well ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park — Seoul's stunning mountain national park offering winter hiking trails with snow-dusted peaks. Take the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail for panoramic views of Seoul. Dress in proper winter hiking gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the Dongdaemun area for a final shopping session. Explore the Dongdaemun Design Plaza market and pick up last-minute Korean souvenirs, fashion, and K-beauty products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Gangnam — explore the vibrant nightlife of Apgujeong and Cheongdam-dong. Visit a rooftop bar for final panoramic views of Seoul's glittering skyline.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store kimbap and hot coffee before the hike — a quintessential Korean hiking tradition
meals.lunch: Post-hike warm meal at a traditional doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean stew) restaurant near Bukhansan
meals.dinner: Kwon Sooksoo — elegant Korean fine dining in Cheongdam-dong, celebrating traditional Korean flavors with refined modern presentation for a memorable farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan requires proper winter hiking boots and warm layers. Trails can be icy — bring microspikes if available. The hike to Baegundae Peak takes approximately 3–4 hours round trip. Return to the city by early afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — revisit a favorite neighborhood or café for a leisurely breakfast. Last-minute shopping at a nearby convenience store or pharmacy for Korean skincare products and snacks to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer to Incheon International Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for check-in, duty-free shopping, and security. Incheon Airport's duty-free zone is world-class — browse Korean cosmetics, food gifts, and luxury goods.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Korean culture, cuisine, and luxury experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast at a local restaurant near the hotel — doenjang jjigae, steamed rice, and banchan (side dishes) for an authentic send-off
meals.lunch: Incheon Airport — dine at one of the premium airport restaurants such as Korean Air's Morning Calm lounge or a sit-down Korean restaurant in the departure terminal
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11am — store luggage at the hotel if needed for a final morning activity. The AREX Express Train from Bupyeong to Incheon Airport takes approximately 30–40 minutes. Incheon Airport is consistently rated the world's best airport — arrive early to enjoy the duty-free experience.
